questions.text: Let $A=\{(\alpha, \beta)\in\mathbf{R}\times\mathbf{R} : |\alpha-1|\le4 \text{ and } |\beta-5|\le6\}$ and $B=\{(\alpha, \beta)\in\mathbf{R}\times\mathbf{R} : 16(\alpha-2)^2+9(\beta-6)^2\le144\}$. Then
questions.sol:
A is the rectangle $-3\le\alpha\le5$, $-1\le\beta\le11$.
B is the region inside the ellipse $\dfrac{(\alpha-2)^2}{9}+\dfrac{(\beta-6)^2}{16}\le1$, which lies within $-1\le\alpha\le5$, $2\le\beta\le10$.
So $B\subset A$ (and $A\not\subset B$, e.g. the corner $(-3, -1)$).

questions.text: If the range of the function $f(x)=\dfrac{5-x}{x^2-3x+2}$, $x\ne1, 2$, is $(-\infty, \alpha]\cup[\beta, \infty)$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$y=\dfrac{5-x}{x^2-3x+2}\iff yx^2+(1-3y)x+(2y-5)=0$ must have a real root $x\ne1, 2$.
Discriminant: $(1-3y)^2-4y(2y-5)=y^2+14y+1\ge0$, so $y\le-7-4\sqrt3$ or $y\ge-7+4\sqrt3$ (the excluded $x=1, 2$ do not satisfy the equation, and $y=0$ comes from $x=5$).
$\alpha^2+\beta^2=(7+4\sqrt3)^2+(7-4\sqrt3)^2=2(49+48)=194$.

questions.text: The number of real roots of the equation $x|x-2|+3|x-3|+1=0$ is :
questions.sol:
$x\ge3$: $x^2+x-8=0$ gives $x=\dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt{33}}{2}$, neither $\ge3$.
$2\le x<3$: $x^2-5x+10=0$ has no real roots.
$x<2$: $-x^2-x+10=0$, i.e. $x=\dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt{41}}{2}$; only $\dfrac{-1-\sqrt{41}}{2}$ is less than 2.
Exactly 1 real root.

questions.text: If the locus of $z\in\mathbf{C}$, such that $\text{Re}\left(\dfrac{z-1}{2z+i}\right)+\text{Re}\left(\dfrac{\bar z-1}{2\bar z-i}\right)=2$, is a circle of radius r and center $(a, b)$, then $\dfrac{15ab}{r^2}$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
The second fraction is the conjugate of the first, so the condition is $\text{Re}\,\dfrac{z-1}{2z+i}=1$.
With $z=x+iy$: $\text{Re}=\dfrac{2x(x-1)+y(2y+1)}{4x^2+(2y+1)^2}=1\Rightarrow x^2+y^2+x+\dfrac32y+\dfrac12=0$.
Centre $\left(-\dfrac12, -\dfrac34\right)$, $r^2=\dfrac14+\dfrac9{16}-\dfrac12=\dfrac5{16}$.
$\dfrac{15ab}{r^2}=\dfrac{15\cdot\frac38}{\frac5{16}}=18$.

questions.text:
Let the system of equations
$x+5y-z=1$
$4x+3y-3z=7$
$24x+y+\lambda z=\mu$
$\lambda, \mu\in\mathbf{R}$, have infinitely many solutions. Then the number of the solutions of this system, if $x, y, z$ are integers and satisfy $7\le x+y+z\le77$, is :
questions.sol:
For infinitely many solutions the third equation must be a combination of the first two: $-4\times$(first) $+\,7\times$(second) gives $24x+y-17z=45$ ($\lambda=-17$, $\mu=45$).
Solving the first two: $z=3+17y$, $x=4+12y$. Integer $x$ and $z$ need $12y$ and $17y$ integers, so $y=t\in\mathbf{Z}$.
$x+y+z=7+30t$, and $7\le7+30t\le77$ gives $t=0, 1, 2$: 3 solutions.

questions.text: Let p be the number of all triangles that can be formed by joining the vertices of a regular polygon P of n sides and q be the number of all quadrilaterals that can be formed by joining the vertices of P. If $p+q=126$, then the eccentricity of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}{n}=1$ is :
questions.sol:
$p+q=\binom n3+\binom n4=\binom{n+1}{4}=126=\binom94$, so $n=8$.
For $\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}{8}=1$: $e=\sqrt{1-\dfrac8{16}}=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$.

questions.text: Let a random variable X take values 0, 1, 2, 3 with $P(X=0)=P(X=1)=p$, $P(X=2)=P(X=3)$ and $E(X^2)=2E(X)$. Then the value of $8p-1$ is :
questions.sol:
Let $P(X=2)=P(X=3)=q$, so $2p+2q=1$.
$E(X)=p+5q$ and $E(X^2)=p+13q$; $p+13q=2p+10q\Rightarrow p=3q$.
$8q=1$, $q=\dfrac18$, $p=\dfrac38$, so $8p-1=2$.

questions.text: A bag contains 19 unbiased coins and one coin with head on both sides. One coin drawn at random is tossed and head turns up. If the probability that the drawn coin was unbiased, is $\dfrac mn$, $\gcd(m, n)=1$, then $n^2-m^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
By Bayes' theorem: $P(\text{unbiased}\mid H)=\dfrac{\frac{19}{20}\cdot\frac12}{\frac{19}{20}\cdot\frac12+\frac1{20}\cdot1}=\dfrac{19}{21}$.
$n^2-m^2=441-361=80$.

questions.text: If the orthocenter of the triangle formed by the lines $y=x+1$, $y=4x-8$ and $y=mx+c$ is at $(3, -1)$, then $m-c$ is :
questions.sol:
The first two lines meet at $A(3, 4)$. The altitude from A passes through $H(3, -1)$, so it is the line $x=3$; the opposite side is therefore horizontal: $m=0$, $y=c$.
B $=(c-1, c)$ on $y=x+1$. The altitude from B is perpendicular to $y=4x-8$ (slope $-\frac14$) and passes through H: $\dfrac{-1-c}{3-(c-1)}=-\dfrac14\Rightarrow c=0$.
$m-c=0$.

questions.text: Let the length of a latus rectum of an ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ be 10. If its eccentricity is the minimum value of the function $f(t)=t^2+t+\dfrac{11}{12}$, $t\in\mathbf{R}$, then $a^2+b^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$f$ is least at $t=-\dfrac12$: $e=\dfrac14-\dfrac12+\dfrac{11}{12}=\dfrac23$.
$\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=10\Rightarrow b^2=5a$, and $b^2=a^2(1-e^2)=\dfrac{5a^2}{9}$. So $a=9$, $b^2=45$.
$a^2+b^2=81+45=126$.

questions.text: Let $e_1$ and $e_2$ be the eccentricities of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{b^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{25}=1$ and the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, respectively. If $b<5$ and $e_1e_2=1$, then the eccentricity of the ellipse having its axes along the coordinate axes and passing through all four foci (two of the ellipse and two of the hyperbola) is :
questions.sol:
$e_1^2=1-\dfrac{b^2}{25}$, $e_2^2=1+\dfrac{b^2}{16}$. $e_1^2e_2^2=1$ gives $b^2\left(\dfrac1{16}-\dfrac1{25}\right)=\dfrac{b^4}{400}$, so $b^2=9$.
Foci: ellipse $(0, \pm4)$, hyperbola $(\pm5, 0)$.
The ellipse through them is $\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1$, with $e=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{16}{25}}=\dfrac35$.

questions.text: The number of solutions of the equation $\cos2\theta\cos\dfrac\theta2+\cos\dfrac{5\theta}{2}=2\cos^3\dfrac{5\theta}{2}$ in $\left[-\dfrac\pi2, \dfrac\pi2\right]$ is :
questions.sol:
$\cos2\theta\cos\dfrac\theta2=\dfrac12\left(\cos\dfrac{5\theta}{2}+\cos\dfrac{3\theta}{2}\right)$ and $2\cos^3A=\dfrac12(\cos3A+3\cos A)$ with $A=\dfrac{5\theta}{2}$.
The equation reduces to $\cos\dfrac{3\theta}{2}=\cos\dfrac{15\theta}{2}$, so $6\theta=2k\pi$ or $9\theta=2k\pi$.
In $\left[-\frac\pi2, \frac\pi2\right]$: $\theta=0, \pm\dfrac\pi3$ and $\theta=\pm\dfrac{2\pi}9, \pm\dfrac{4\pi}9$: 7 solutions.

questions.text: Let $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ be the vectors of the same magnitude such that $\dfrac{|\vec a+\vec b|+|\vec a-\vec b|}{|\vec a+\vec b|-|\vec a-\vec b|}=\sqrt2+1$. Then $\dfrac{|\vec a+\vec b|^2}{|\vec a|^2}$ is :
questions.sol:
Let $u=|\vec a+\vec b|$, $v=|\vec a-\vec b|$. Then $\dfrac uv=\dfrac{\sqrt2+2}{\sqrt2}=1+\sqrt2$, so $u^2=(3+2\sqrt2)v^2$.
Since $|\vec a|=|\vec b|$, $u^2+v^2=4|\vec a|^2$, giving $u^2=\dfrac{4(3+2\sqrt2)}{4+2\sqrt2}|\vec a|^2=(2+\sqrt2)|\vec a|^2$.
Ratio $=2+\sqrt2$.

questions.text: If the equation of the line passing through the point $\left(0, -\dfrac12, 0\right)$ and perpendicular to the lines $\vec r=\lambda\left(\hat i+a\hat j+b\hat k\right)$ and $\vec r=\left(\hat i-\hat j-6\hat k\right)+\mu\left(-b\hat i+a\hat j+5\hat k\right)$ is $\dfrac{x-1}{-2}=\dfrac{y+4}{d}=\dfrac{z-c}{-4}$, then $a+b+c+d$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\left(0, -\frac12, 0\right)$ lies on the line: $\dfrac{-1}{-2}=\dfrac{7/2}{d}=\dfrac{-c}{-4}$, so $d=7$, $c=2$.
Perpendicularity of $(-2, 7, -4)$ to $(1, a, b)$ and $(-b, a, 5)$: $7a-4b=2$ and $7a+2b=20$, so $b=3$, $a=2$.
$a+b+c+d=2+3+2+7=14$.

questions.text: Let $f : \mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ be a polynomial function of degree four having extreme values at $x=4$ and $x=5$. If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{f(x)}{x^2}=5$, then $f(2)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
The limit forces $f(x)=5x^2+px^3+qx^4$.
$f^\prime(x)=x(10+3px+4qx^2)$ vanishes at 4 and 5: $4qx^2+3px+10=4q(x-4)(x-5)$, so $80q=10$, $q=\dfrac18$, and $3p=-36q$, $p=-\dfrac32$.
$f(2)=20-12+2=10$.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $(x^2+1)y^\prime-2xy=(x^4+2x^2+1)\cos x$, $y(0)=1$. Then $\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{3}y(x)\,dx$ is :
questions.sol:
Dividing by $(x^2+1)^2$: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{y}{x^2+1}\right)=\cos x$, so $\dfrac{y}{x^2+1}=\sin x+C$; $y(0)=1$ gives $C=1$.
$y=(x^2+1)(1+\sin x)$. The part $(x^2+1)\sin x$ is odd and integrates to zero.
$\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{3}(x^2+1)dx=2(9+3)=24$.

questions.text: If the area of the region $\{(x, y) : 1+x^2\le y\le\min\{x+7, 11-3x\}\}$ is A, then 3A is equal to
questions.sol:
The lines meet at $(1, 8)$; $y=1+x^2$ meets $y=x+7$ at $x=-2$ and $y=11-3x$ at $x=2$.
$A=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{1}(x+6-x^2)dx+\int_{1}^{2}(10-3x-x^2)dx=\frac{27}{2}+\frac{19}{6}=\frac{50}{3}$.
$3A=50$.

questions.text: The sum of the series $2\times1\times{}^{20}C_4-3\times2\times{}^{20}C_5+4\times3\times{}^{20}C_6-5\times4\times{}^{20}C_7+\cdots+18\times17\times{}^{20}C_{20}$, is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
The sum is $S=\displaystyle\sum_{r=4}^{20}(-1)^r(r-2)(r-3)\binom{20}{r}$.
For any polynomial $g$ of degree less than 20, $\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{20}(-1)^rg(r)\binom{20}{r}=0$. The terms $r=2, 3$ are zero; $r=0$ gives $6$ and $r=1$ gives $-40$.
$S=0-6+40=34$.

questions.text: Let the lengths of the transverse and conjugate axes of a hyperbola in standard form be 2a and 2b, respectively, and one focus and the corresponding directrix of this hyperbola be $(-5, 0)$ and $5x+9=0$, respectively. If the product of the focal distances of a point $(\alpha, 2\sqrt5)$ on the hyperbola is p, then 4p is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
$ae=5$ and $\dfrac ae=\dfrac95$, so $a=3$, $e=\dfrac53$, $b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=16$.
$\dfrac{\alpha^2}{9}-\dfrac{20}{16}=1\Rightarrow|\alpha|=\dfrac92$.
Focal distances $e|\alpha|\pm a=7.5\pm3$: $10.5$ and $4.5$, product $p=47.25$, so $4p=189$.

questions.text: For $t>-1$, let $\alpha_t$ and $\beta_t$ be the roots of the equation $\left((t+2)^{1/7}-1\right)x^2+\left((t+2)^{1/6}-1\right)x+\left((t+2)^{1/21}-1\right)=0$. If $\displaystyle\lim_{t\to-1^+}\alpha_t=a$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{t\to-1^+}\beta_t=b$, then $72(a+b)^2$ is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
Put $h=t+1\to0^+$; $(1+h)^{1/k}-1\sim\dfrac hk$. Dividing the equation by $h$, the limiting equation is $\dfrac{x^2}{7}+\dfrac x6+\dfrac1{21}=0$, i.e. $6x^2+7x+2=0$.
$a+b=-\dfrac76$, so $72(a+b)^2=72\cdot\dfrac{49}{36}=98$.

questions.text: If the function $f(x)=\dfrac{\tan(\tan x)-\sin(\sin x)}{\tan x-\sin x}$ is continuous at $x=0$, then $f(0)$ is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
Near 0: $\tan x=x+\dfrac{x^3}3+\cdots$, so $\tan(\tan x)=x+\dfrac{2x^3}{3}+\cdots$; $\sin x=x-\dfrac{x^3}6+\cdots$, so $\sin(\sin x)=x-\dfrac{x^3}{3}+\cdots$.
Numerator $\sim x^3$; denominator $\tan x-\sin x\sim\dfrac{x^3}{2}$.
$f(0)=\lim\limits_{x\to0}f(x)=2$.

questions.text:
The dimension of $\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_0}{\epsilon_0}}$ is equal to that of :
($\mu_0$ = Vacuum permeability and $\epsilon_0$ = Vacuum permittivity)
questions.sol:
$\mu_0$ has units $\text{V s A}^{-1}\text{m}^{-1}$ and $\epsilon_0$ has units $\text{A s V}^{-1}\text{m}^{-1}$.
$\dfrac{\mu_0}{\epsilon_0}$ has units $\text{V}^2\text{A}^{-2}=\Omega^2$, so $\sqrt{\mu_0/\epsilon_0}$ (about $377\ \Omega$, the impedance of free space) has the dimensions of resistance.

questions.text:
A helicopter flying horizontally with a speed of 360 km/h at an altitude of 2 km, drops an object at an instant. The object hits the ground at a point O, 20 s after it is dropped. Displacement of 'O' from the position of helicopter where the object was released is :
(use acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s$^2$ and neglect air resistance)
questions.sol:
Horizontal: $100\ \text{m/s}\times20\ \text{s}=2$ km. Vertical: $\dfrac12\times10\times20^2=2000$ m $=2$ km (the full altitude).
Displacement $=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}=2\sqrt2$ km.

questions.text: Which one of the following forces cannot be expressed in terms of potential energy ?
questions.sol:
A potential energy can be defined only for a conservative force, whose work is independent of path.
Coulomb, gravitational and elastic restoring forces are conservative; friction is not (its work depends on the path).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The radius vector from the Sun to a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time and thus areal velocity of planet is constant.
Reason (R) : For a central force field the angular momentum is a constant.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol:
A central force exerts no torque about the centre, so the angular momentum $L$ of the planet is conserved.
Areal velocity $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{L}{2m}$ is therefore constant (Kepler's second law).
Both are correct and (R) explains (A).

questions.text: A capillary tube of radius 0.1 mm is partly dipped in water (surface tension 70 dyn/cm and glass water contact angle $\approx0^\circ$) with $30^\circ$ inclined with the vertical. The length of water risen in the capillary is ______ cm. (Take g = 9.8 m/s$^2$)
questions.note: Strictly the length is $\dfrac{h}{\cos30^\circ}\approx16.5$ cm; NTA's final key gives $\dfrac{82}{5}=16.4$ cm, the closest option.
questions.sol:
Vertical rise $h=\dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g}=\dfrac{2\times0.07}{10^{-4}\times1000\times9.8}=0.1429$ m $=14.29$ cm.
The tube is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the vertical, so the length of the water column is $l=\dfrac{h}{\cos30^\circ}=\dfrac{14.29}{0.866}\approx16.5$ cm.
The nearest option is $\dfrac{82}{5}=16.4$ cm.

questions.text:
The helium and argon are put in the flask at the same room temperature (300 K). The ratio of average kinetic energies (per molecule) of helium and argon is :
(Give : Molar mass of helium = 4 g/mol, Molar mass of argon = 40 g/mol)
questions.sol: The average translational kinetic energy per molecule is $\dfrac32kT$, independent of the molar mass. Both are monoatomic at the same temperature, so the ratio is 1 : 1.

Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
(A) Isothermal(I) $\Delta W$ (work done) $=0$
(B) Adiabatic(II) $\Delta Q$ (supplied heat) $=0$
(C) Isobaric(III) $\Delta U$ (change in internal energy) $\ne0$

questions.text: The equation of a wave travelling on a string is $y=\sin[20\pi x+10\pi t]$, where $x$ and t are distance and time in SI units. The minimum distance between two points having the same oscillating speed is :
questions.sol:
$k=20\pi$ m$^{-1}$, so $\lambda=\dfrac{2\pi}{k}=0.1$ m $=10$ cm.
The particle speed is $10\pi|\cos(20\pi x+10\pi t)|$. Two points have the same speed at every instant when their phases differ by $\pi$, i.e. when they are $\dfrac\lambda2$ apart.
Minimum distance $=5.0$ cm.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Magnetic monopoles do not exist.
Reason (R) : Magnetic field lines are continuous and form closed loops.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol:
No isolated magnetic pole has ever been found, and Gauss's law for magnetism (zero net flux through any closed surface) expresses this.
Since there are no sources or sinks of $\vec B$, the field lines cannot start or end anywhere and so form closed loops. NTA's key treats (R) as the correct explanation of (A).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The outer body of an air craft is made of metal which protects persons sitting inside from lightning-strikes.
Reason (R) : The electric field inside the cavity enclosed by a conductor is zero.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol:
The field inside a charge-free cavity of a conductor is zero whatever the outside charges (electrostatic shielding). The metal body therefore shields the passengers; the charge of a strike stays on the outer surface.
Both are correct and (R) explains (A).

questions.text: A mirror is used to produce an image with magnification of $\dfrac14$. If the distance between object and its image is 40 cm, then the focal length of the mirror is ______.
questions.sol:
An erect image with $m=+\dfrac14$ is formed by a convex mirror: object at distance $u$ in front, image $\dfrac u4$ behind, so $u+\dfrac u4=40$ and $u=32$ cm, $v=+8$ cm.
$\dfrac1f=\dfrac1v+\dfrac1u=\dfrac18-\dfrac1{32}=\dfrac3{32}$, so $f=\dfrac{32}{3}\approx10.7$ cm.
(A real inverted image with $m=-\frac14$ from a concave mirror gives the same magnitude.)

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Refractive index of glass is higher than that of air.
Reason (R) : Optical density of a medium is directly proportionate to its mass density which results in a proportionate refractive index.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol:
Glass ($n\approx1.5$) has a higher refractive index than air ($n\approx1$): (A) is correct.
Optical density is not proportional to mass density (for example, turpentine is less dense than water but has a higher refractive index): (R) is not correct.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A transparent block A having refractive index $\mu=1.25$ is surrounded by another medium of refractive index $\mu=1.0$ as shown in figure. A light ray is incident on the flat face of the block with incident angle $\theta$ as shown in figure. What is the maximum value of $\theta$ for which light suffers total internal reflection at the top surface of the block ?
questions.sol:
At the side face: $\sin\theta=1.25\sin r$. The ray meets the top face at $90^\circ-r$ to its normal.
Total internal reflection there needs $\sin(90^\circ-r)\ge\dfrac1{1.25}=0.8$, i.e. $\cos r\ge0.8$, $\sin r\le0.6$.
So $\sin\theta\le1.25\times0.6=0.75$: $\theta_{max}=\sin^{-1}(3/4)$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A photoemissive substance is illuminated with a radiation of wavelength $\lambda_i$ so that it releases electrons with de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_e$. The longest wavelength of radiation that can emit photoelectron is $\lambda_o$. Expression for de-Broglie wavelength is given by :
(m : mass of the electron, h : Planck's constant and c : speed of light)
questions.sol:
Maximum kinetic energy $K=hc\left(\dfrac1{\lambda_i}-\dfrac1{\lambda_o}\right)$ and $p=\sqrt{2mK}$.
$\lambda_e=\dfrac hp=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mhc\left(\frac1{\lambda_i}-\frac1{\lambda_o}\right)}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{2mc\left(\frac1{\lambda_i}-\frac1{\lambda_o}\right)}}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The density of the copper $\left({}^{64}_{29}\text{Cu}\right)$ nucleus is greater than that of the carbon $\left({}^{12}_{6}\text{C}\right)$ nucleus.
Reason (R) : The nucleus of mass number A has a radius proportional to $A^{1/3}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol: $R=R_0A^{1/3}$ (R correct), so the volume is proportional to $A$, as is the mass. Nuclear density is therefore the same for all nuclei: (A) is not correct.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Consider the following logic circuit.
The output is Y = 0 when :
questions.sol:
The AND gate gives $AB$; the OR gate receives B and $\bar A$, giving $B+\bar A$. The final NAND gives $Y=\overline{AB\,(B+\bar A)}=\overline{AB}$, since $AB(B+\bar A)=AB$.
$Y=0$ only when $A=1$ and $B=1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: M and R be the mass and radius of a disc. A small disc of radius R/3 is removed from the bigger disc as shown in figure. The moment of inertia of remaining part of bigger disc about an axis AB passing through the centre O and perpendicular to the plane of disc is $\dfrac4x$MR$^2$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.sol:
The removed disc has mass $\dfrac M9$ (area ratio) and its centre O$^\prime$ is $\dfrac{2R}{3}$ from O.
About the perpendicular axis through O: $I_{small}=\dfrac M9\cdot\dfrac{(R/3)^2}{2}+\dfrac M9\left(\dfrac{2R}3\right)^2=\dfrac{MR^2}{162}+\dfrac{4MR^2}{81}=\dfrac{MR^2}{18}$.
$I=\dfrac{MR^2}2-\dfrac{MR^2}{18}=\dfrac49MR^2$, so $x=9$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: Two cylindrical rods A and B made of different materials, are joined in a straight line. The ratios of lengths, radii and thermal conductivites of these rods are: $\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}=\dfrac12$, $\dfrac{r_A}{r_B}=2$ and $\dfrac{K_A}{K_B}=\dfrac12$. The free ends of rods A and B are maintained at 400 K, 200 K, respectively. The temperature of rods interface is ______ K, when equilibrium is established.
questions.sol:
Thermal resistance $R=\dfrac{L}{KA}$: $\dfrac{R_A}{R_B}=\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}\cdot\dfrac{K_B}{K_A}\cdot\left(\dfrac{r_B}{r_A}\right)^2=\dfrac12\cdot2\cdot\dfrac14=\dfrac14$.
In series the 200 K drop divides as 1 : 4, so 40 K across A.
Interface temperature $=400-40=360$ K.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An inductor of reactance 100 $\Omega$, a capacitor of reactance 50 $\Omega$, and a resistor of resistance 50 $\Omega$ are connected in series with an AC source of 10 V, 50 Hz. Average power dissipated by the circuit is ______ W.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor has charge $5\times10^{-6}$ C. A dielectric slab is inserted between the plates and almost fills the space between the plates. If the induced charge on one face of the slab is $4\times10^{-6}$ C then the dielectric constant of the slab is ______.
questions.sol: Induced charge $q^\prime=q\left(1-\dfrac1K\right)$: $4=5\left(1-\dfrac1K\right)$, so $\dfrac1K=\dfrac15$ and $K=5$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The electric field in a region is given by $\vec E=\left(2\hat i+4\hat j+6\hat k\right)\times10^3$ N/C. The flux of the field through a rectangular surface parallel to $x$-$z$ plane is 6.0 Nm$^2$C$^{-1}$. The area of the surface is ______ cm$^2$.
questions.sol:
A surface parallel to the $x$-$z$ plane has its normal along $\hat j$, so $\Phi=E_yA=4\times10^3A$.
$A=\dfrac{6.0}{4\times10^3}=1.5\times10^{-3}$ m$^2=15$ cm$^2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The extra stability of half-filled subshell is due to :
(A) Symmetrical distribution of electrons
(B) Smaller coulombic repulsion energy
(C) The presence of electrons with the same spin in non-degenerate orbitals
(D) Larger exchange energy
(E) Relatively smaller shielding of electrons by one another
Indentify the correct statements :
questions.sol:
Half-filled subshells are stable because of the symmetrical distribution of electrons (A) and the large exchange energy of electrons with parallel spins (D); electrons of parallel spin keep apart, lowering the repulsion (B); and electrons in the same subshell shield one another relatively little, so they are held more strongly (E).
(C) is wrong: the orbitals of a subshell are degenerate.
(A), (B), (D) and (E).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct statement amongst the following is :
options: The term 'standard state' implies that the temperature is 0$^\circ$C.
The standard state of a pure gas is the pure gas at a pressure of 1 bar and temperature 273 K.
questions.sol:
The standard state fixes the pressure (1 bar) but not the temperature, so (1) and (2) are wrong.
The standard enthalpy of formation is zero for an element in its reference state at any temperature: $\mathrm{O_2(g)}$ qualifies (4), atomic O(g) does not (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The hydration energies of $\mathrm{K^+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ are $-x$ and $-y$ kJ/mol respectively. If lattice energy of KCl is $-z$ kJ/mol, then the heat of solution of KCl is :
questions.sol:
Dissolving = breaking the lattice (reverse of lattice formation, $+z$) then hydrating the ions ($-x-y$).
$\Delta H_{sol}=z-(x+y)$ kJ/mol.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
(A) Solution of chloroform and acetone(I) Minimum boiling azeotrope
(B) Solution of ethanol and water(II) Dimerizes
(C) Solution of benzene and toluene(III) Maximum boiling azeotrope
(D) Solution of acetic acid in benzene(IV) $\Delta V_{mix}=0$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Chloroform-acetone: negative deviation (hydrogen bonding between them), maximum boiling azeotrope (III). Ethanol-water: positive deviation, minimum boiling azeotrope (I). Benzene-toluene: nearly ideal, $\Delta V_{mix}=0$ (IV). Acetic acid in benzene dimerises through hydrogen bonds (II).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Liquid A and B form an ideal solution. The vapour pressures of pure liquids A and B are 350 and 750 mm Hg respectively at the same temperature. If $x_A$ and $x_B$ are the mole fraction of A and B in solution while $y_A$ and $y_B$ are the mole fraction of A and B in vapour phase then,
questions.sol:
By Raoult's and Dalton's laws, $\dfrac{y_A}{y_B}=\dfrac{p_A^\circ x_A}{p_B^\circ x_B}=\dfrac{350}{750}\cdot\dfrac{x_A}{x_B}$.
So $\dfrac{x_A}{x_B}>\dfrac{y_A}{y_B}$: the vapour is richer in the more volatile B.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
1 M aqueous solutions of each of $\mathrm{Cu(NO_3)_2}$, $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$, $\mathrm{Hg_2(NO_3)_2}$; $\mathrm{Mg(NO_3)_2}$ are electrolysed using inert electrodes. Given : $E^\theta_{\mathrm{Ag^+/Ag}}=0.80$ V, $E^\theta_{\mathrm{Hg_2^{2+}/Hg}}=0.79$ V, $E^\theta_{\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}}=0.24$ V and $E^\theta_{\mathrm{Mg^{2+}/Mg}}=-2.37$ V.
Statement (I) : With increasing voltage, the sequence of deposition of metals on the cathode will be Ag, Hg and Cu.
Statement (II) : Magnesium will not be deposited at cathode instead oxygen gas will be evolved at the cathode.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Ions with higher reduction potential are discharged first: Ag (0.80 V), then Hg (0.79 V), then Cu. Statement I is correct.
$\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ is not reduced in water; water is reduced instead, giving hydrogen gas at the cathode (oxygen is evolved at the anode). Statement II is incorrect.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$\mathrm{A(g)\rightarrow B(g)+C(g)}$ is a first order reaction.
Timet$\infty$
$p_{system}$$p_t$$p_\infty$
The reaction was started with reactant A only. Which of the following expression is correct for rate constant k ?
questions.sol:
With initial pressure $p_0$: $p_\infty=2p_0$, and at time t, $p_t=p_0+x$, so $p_A=p_0-x=2p_0-p_t=p_\infty-p_t$.
$k=\dfrac1t\ln\dfrac{p_0}{p_A}=\dfrac1t\ln\dfrac{p_\infty}{2(p_\infty-p_t)}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In $\mathrm{SO_2}$, $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$ and $\mathrm{N_3^-}$ the hybridizations at the central atom are respectively :
questions.sol: $\mathrm{SO_2}$: S has 2 bonded atoms and 1 lone pair, $sp^2$. $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$: N has 2 bonded atoms and 1 lone pair, $sp^2$. $\mathrm{N_3^-}$: the central N is linear with no lone pair, $sp$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Choose the incorrect trend in the atomic radii (r) of the elements.
questions.sol:
Atomic radius decreases across a period, so Mg (160 pm) is larger than Al (143 pm): $r_{\text{Mg}}<r_{\text{Al}}$ is the incorrect trend.
The others are correct: At is smaller than Cs (same period), Rb smaller than Cs (down the group), Br smaller than K.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
The correct statements from the following are :
(A) $\mathrm{Tl^{3+}}$ is a powerful oxidising agent
(B) $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ does not get reduced easily
(C) Both $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Tl^{3+}}$ are very stable in solution
(D) $\mathrm{Tl^+}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{Tl^{3+}}$
(E) $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Tl^+}$ are highly stable
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Down group 13 the inert pair effect makes the +1 state increasingly stable: for thallium +1 is more stable than +3, so $\mathrm{Tl^{3+}}$ is readily reduced and is a strong oxidising agent (A, D correct).
For aluminium +3 is the stable state, and $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ is hard to reduce (B correct). So $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Tl^+}$ are the stable ions (E correct), while $\mathrm{Tl^{3+}}$ is not (C wrong).
(A), (B), (D) and (E).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: 'X' is the number of acidic oxides among $\mathrm{VO_2}$, $\mathrm{V_2O_3}$, $\mathrm{CrO_3}$, $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$ and $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$. The primary valency of cobalt in $\mathrm{[Co(H_2NCH_2CH_2NH_2)_3)]_2\,(SO_4)_3}$ is Y. The value of X + Y is ______.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{V_2O_3}$ is basic, $\mathrm{VO_2}$ and $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$ are amphoteric, and $\mathrm{CrO_3}$ and $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$ are acidic: X = 2.
In $\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]_2(SO_4)_3}$ cobalt is +3, so its primary valency Y = 3.
X + Y = 5.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The number of unpaired electrons responsible for the paramagnetic nature of the following complex species are respectively :
$\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ $d^5$, low spin, 1. $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$: $d^5$ high spin, 5. $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$: $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ $d^6$ high spin, 4. $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$: $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ $d^4$ low spin, 2.
1, 5, 4, 2.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
Complex		List - II
Primary valency and Secondary valency
(A) $\mathrm{[Co(en)_2Cl_2]Cl}$(I) 36
(B) $\mathrm{[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl(NO_2)]}$(II) 34
(C) $\mathrm{Hg[Co(SCN)_4]}$(III) 26
(D) $\mathrm{[Mg(EDTA)]^{2-}}$(IV) 24
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.note: Strictly, cobalt is +2 in $\mathrm{Hg[Co(SCN)_4]}$ (primary valency 2, secondary valency 4, i.e. (IV) again), so no option is exactly right. NTA's final key gives option (3), which is the only option that matches (A), (B) and (D) correctly.
questions.sol:
Primary valency = oxidation state of the metal; secondary valency = coordination number.
(A) $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$, two bidentate en and two Cl: 3 and 6 (I). (B) $\mathrm{Pt^{2+}}$, four monodentate ligands: 2 and 4 (IV). (D) $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ with hexadentate EDTA: 2 and 6 (III).
(C) has four SCN ligands (secondary valency 4); by elimination it is matched with (II), giving option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Mixture of 1 g each of chlorobenzene, aniline and benzoic acid is dissolved in 50 mL ethyl acetate and placed in a separating funnel. 5 M NaOH (30 mL) was added in the same funnel. The funnel was shaken vigorously and then kept aside. The ethyl acetate layer in the funnel contains :
questions.sol:
NaOH converts benzoic acid into water-soluble sodium benzoate, which passes into the aqueous layer.
Chlorobenzene (neutral) and aniline (basic, not affected by NaOH) stay in the ethyl acetate layer.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Statement I: in the cis isomers the two C-X bond moments add; C-Cl bonds are more polar than C-Br bonds, so cis-1,2-dichloroethene is more polar than cis-1,2-dibromoethene. Correct.
Statement II: trans-1,2-dibromoethene does have the lower boiling point, but its bond moments cancel, so it is non-polar, i.e. less polar than the cis isomer. Incorrect.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The number of optically active products obtained from the complete ozonolysis of the given compound is :
questions.sol:
Ozonolysis cleaves all three C=C bonds, giving two molecules of $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$ and two of $\mathrm{OHC{-}CH(CH_3){-}CHO}$.
In 2-methylpropanedial the central carbon carries two identical CHO groups, so it is not a stereocentre; ethanal is achiral too.
Number of optically active products $=0$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Electron-withdrawing nitro groups at the ortho and para positions make the C-Cl bond progressively easier to substitute:
chlorobenzene needs NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm (IV); 4-nitrochlorobenzene needs 443 K (III); 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene needs 368 K (II); 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene reacts with warm water (I).
(A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
"P" is an optically active compound with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O}$. When 'P' is treated with 2, 4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, it gives a positive test. However, in presence of Tollens reagent, "P" gives a negative test.
Predict the structure of "P".
questions.sol:
A positive 2,4-DNP test with a negative Tollens test means P is a ketone, and it must be chiral.
$\mathrm{CH_3COCH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3}$ (3-methylpentan-2-one) has a stereocentre carrying H, $\mathrm{CH_3}$, $\mathrm{C_2H_5}$ and $\mathrm{COCH_3}$. Option (1) and option (4) are achiral ketones; option (3) is an aldehyde.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The descending order of basicity of following amines is :
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than aryl amines; in water $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH}$ (E) $>$ $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$ (D).
Among the anilines, the electron-donating OMe group raises basicity (B $>$ A) and the electron-withdrawing $\mathrm{NO_2}$ group lowers it strongly (C weakest).
E $>$ D $>$ B $>$ A $>$ C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : On hydrolysis, oligo peptides give rise to fewer number of $\alpha$-amino acids while proteins give rise to a large number of $\beta$-amino acids.
Statement (II) : Natural proteins are denatured by acids which convert the water soluble form of fibrous proteins to their water insoluble form.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Statement I: proteins, like oligopeptides, are built from $\alpha$-amino acids, not $\beta$-amino acids. Incorrect.
Statement II: on denaturation globular proteins (water soluble) change into fibrous, insoluble forms; fibrous proteins are already insoluble, so the statement as written is incorrect.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Butane reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water following the equation given below.
$\mathrm{C_4H_{10}(g)+\dfrac{13}{2}O_2(g)\rightarrow4CO_2(g)+5H_2O(\mathit{l})}$
If 174.0 kg of butane is mixed with 320.0 kg of $\mathrm{O_2}$, the volume of water formed in liters is ______. (Nearest integer)
[Given : (a) Molar mass of C, H, O are 12, 1, 16 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively, (b) Density of water = 1g mL$^{-1}$]
questions.sol:
Butane: $\dfrac{174000}{58}=3000$ mol, needing $19500$ mol $\mathrm{O_2}$; only $\dfrac{320000}{32}=10000$ mol $\mathrm{O_2}$ is present, so $\mathrm{O_2}$ is limiting.
Water formed $=10000\times\dfrac{5}{13/2}=7692.3$ mol $=138461$ g, i.e. about 138 L.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
One litre buffer solution was prepared by adding 0.10 mol each of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ in deionised water. The change in pH on addition of 0.05 mol of HCl to the above solution is ______ $\times10^{-2}$. (Nearest integer)
Given : $\mathrm{p}K_b$ of $\mathrm{NH_3}=4.745$ and $\log_{10}3=0.477$
questions.sol:
Initially pOH $=\mathrm{p}K_b+\log\dfrac{0.10}{0.10}=4.745$.
HCl converts 0.05 mol $\mathrm{NH_3}$ into $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$: base 0.05, salt 0.15, pOH $=4.745+\log3=5.222$.
The pH falls by $0.477=47.7\times10^{-2}$, i.e. 48.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The number of paramagnetic metal complex species among $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ and $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$ with same number of unpaired electrons is ______.
questions.sol:
Unpaired electrons: $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ 0, $\mathrm{[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$ 0, $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$ 4 (high spin $d^4$), $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ 2, $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ 4, $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ 1, $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$ 5.
Only $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$ and $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ are paramagnetic with the same number (4): 2.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
In Dumas' method 292 mg of an organic compound released 50 mL of nitrogen gas $\mathrm{(N_2)}$ at 300 K temperature and 715 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of 'N' in the organic compound is ______% (Nearest integer)
(Aqueous tension at 300 K = 15 mm Hg)
questions.sol:
Pressure of dry $\mathrm{N_2}=715-15=700$ mm Hg.
Volume at STP $=50\times\dfrac{700}{760}\times\dfrac{273}{300}=41.9$ mL; mass of N $=\dfrac{28\times41.9}{22400}$ g $=52.4$ mg.
% N $=\dfrac{52.4}{292}\times100=17.9\approx18$.

questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Identify the structure of the final product (D) in the following sequence of the reactions :
Total number of $sp^2$ hybridised carbon atoms in product D is ______.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{PCl_5}$ turns acetophenone into the gem-dichloride $\mathrm{PhCCl_2CH_3}$ (A). Three equivalents of $\mathrm{NaNH_2}$ eliminate two HCl and deprotonate the terminal alkyne: $\mathrm{PhC{\equiv}C^-Na^+}$ (B). Acidifying gives phenylacetylene (C).
Hydroboration-oxidation of a terminal alkyne gives the aldehyde $\mathrm{PhCH_2CHO}$ (D).
$sp^2$ carbons: 6 in the ring + 1 in CHO $=7$.
